title: A strictly standard element inverts to a smooth algebra
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] and let $a\in A$ be strictly standard in $A$ over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element]. Then the localization $A_a$ of $A$ at $\{1,a,a^2,\dots\}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], an $R$-algebra via $R\to A\to A_a$, is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07CA (lemma-elkik, line 253), first paragraph of its proof (lines 261-276: 'Assume a is strictly standard in A over R. We claim that A_a is smooth over R')

proof.text: (Setup and the matrix of the conormal map.) By [def-weil-pbc-strictly-standard-element] (2) there are a presentation $A\cong R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$, an integer $0\le c\le\min(n,m)$ and elements $a_I\in A$ ($I\subseteq\{1,\dots,n\}$, $|I|=c$) such that $a=\sum_Ia_I\det(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}$ in $A$ and $af_{c+j}\in(f_1,\dots,f_c)+(f_1,\dots,f_m)^2$ for $j=1,\dots,m-c$. By [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] the presentation is a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\alpha:P=R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] with kernel $I_0=(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ (we write $I_0$ for the ideal, as $I$ indexes minors); write $[g]$ for the class in $I_0/I_0^2$ of $g\in I_0$, an $A$-module through $\alpha$. Let $\Omega=A\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ [def-weil-module-base-change] and $\mathrm d_\alpha:I_0/I_0^2\to\Omega$, $[g]\mapsto1\otimes\mathrm dg$, the $A$-linear map of [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-split-conormal-smooth] (the degree-one map of $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)$ in [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent]). By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis], $\Omega_{P/R}$ is free on $\mathrm dx_1,\dots,\mathrm dx_n$ and $\mathrm dg=\sum_i(\partial g/\partial x_i)\mathrm dx_i$; hence ($A\otimes_P-$ commutes with finite direct sums and $A\otimes_PP=A$) $\Omega$ is a free $A$-module with basis $e_i=1\otimes\mathrm dx_i$ and $\mathrm d_\alpha[g]=\sum_i\alpha(\partial g/\partial x_i)e_i$. Let $\varepsilon:A^{\oplus c}\to I_0/I_0^2$, $(s_1,\dots,s_c)\mapsto\sum_{j\le c}s_j[f_j]$. In the standard basis of $A^{\oplus c}$ and the basis $(e_i)$ of $\Omega$, the $A$-linear map $\mathrm d_\alpha\circ\varepsilon$ has the $n\times c$ matrix $M$ [def-weil-matrix] with $M_{ij}=\alpha(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CA (lemma-elkik), lines 263-267 ('let A = R[x_1..x_n]/(f_1..f_m), c ... be as in Definition 07C7. Write I = (f_1..f_m) so that the naive cotangent complex ... is given by I/I^2 -> (+) A dx_i')

proof.text: (Equation (strictly-standard-one) gives a left inverse up to $a$; Smoothing Lemma 07ET, a special case of Algebra Lemma 07DQ.) For $I=\{i_1<\dots<i_c\}$ the $c\times c$ submatrix $M_I$ of $M$ formed by the rows $i_1,\dots,i_c$ [def-weil-submatrix] has entries $(M_I)_{kj}=\alpha(\partial f_j/\partial x_{i_k})$: it is the transpose of the image under $\alpha$ of the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)_{j=1,\dots,c,\ i\in I}$ of step 1. By the formula of [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], a polynomial with integer coefficients in the entries, $\det$ commutes with the ring map $\alpha$, and $\det N^{\mathsf T}=\det N$ (substitute $\sigma\mapsto\sigma^{-1}$, $\operatorname{sgn}\sigma^{-1}=\operatorname{sgn}\sigma$). Hence the first condition of step 1 reads $a=\sum_Ia_I\det(M_I)$, i.e. $a$ lies in the ideal of $A$ generated by the $c\times c$ minors of $M$. Since $n\ge c\ge0$, [lem-weil-pbc-matrix-left-inverse-minors] (1), over the ring $A$ with the $n\times c$ matrix $M$ and $f=a$, gives a $c\times n$ matrix $B$ over $A$ with $BM=a\cdot1_{c\times c}$. Let $\psi:\Omega\to A^{\oplus c}$ be the $A$-linear map with matrix $B$ in the bases of step 1; as composition of maps of finite free modules is multiplication of matrices, $\psi\circ\mathrm d_\alpha\circ\varepsilon=a\cdot\mathrm{id}_{A^{\oplus c}}$. (For $c=0$ all of this is about the zero module and holds trivially.)

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07ET (lemma-parse-equation-strictly-standard-one, line 229) and its proof (special case of Algebra, Lemma Tag 07DQ, lemma-matrix-left-inverse, algebra.tex line 2668), cited in the proof of 07CA, lines 270-273

proof.text: (Equation (strictly-standard-two): $(I_0/I_0^2)_a$ is generated by $[f_1],\dots,[f_c]$.) Let $h\in P$ with $\alpha(h)=a$. For $j=1,\dots,m-c$ the second condition of step 1 gives $hf_{c+j}=\sum_{k\le c}p_kf_k+q$ with $p_k\in P$, $q\in I_0^2$, so in $I_0/I_0^2$: $a[f_{c+j}]=[hf_{c+j}]=\sum_{k\le c}\alpha(p_k)[f_k]$. Every $g\in I_0$ is $\sum_{l\le m}p'_lf_l$, so $[g]=\sum_l\alpha(p'_l)[f_l]$: the classes $[f_1],\dots,[f_m]$ generate the $A$-module $I_0/I_0^2$. In the localization $(I_0/I_0^2)_a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], $a$ acts bijectively, so $[f_{c+j}]/1=(1/a)\cdot(a[f_{c+j}])/1=\sum_{k\le c}(\alpha(p_k)/a)\,[f_k]/1$, and every element $x/a^e=(1/a^e)\,x/1$ is an $A_a$-linear combination of $[f_1]/1,\dots,[f_c]/1$. Hence the localization $\varepsilon_a:A_a^{\oplus c}\to(I_0/I_0^2)_a$ of $\varepsilon$, $e_j\mapsto[f_j]/1$, is surjective.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CA (lemma-elkik), lines 268-269 ('Assumption (equation-strictly-standard-two) implies that (I/I^2)_a is generated by the classes of f_1, ..., f_c')

proof.text: ($\mathrm d_\alpha$ becomes split injective after inverting $a$.) Localize at $a$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]: by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] the localization $\varphi_a:M_a\to M'_a$, $m/a^e\mapsto\varphi(m)/a^e$, of an $A$-linear map $\varphi$ is well defined and $A_a$-linear, and visibly $(\varphi\circ\chi)_a=\varphi_a\circ\chi_a$ and $(a\cdot\mathrm{id})_a=a\cdot\mathrm{id}$; also $(A^{\oplus c})_a=A_a^{\oplus c}$ and $\Omega_a$ is free on the $e_i/1$. From step 2, $\psi_a\circ(\mathrm d_\alpha)_a\circ\varepsilon_a=a\cdot\mathrm{id}$, and $a$ is a unit of $A_a$; put $\psi'=a^{-1}\psi_a$, so $\psi'\circ(\mathrm d_\alpha)_a\circ\varepsilon_a=\mathrm{id}_{A_a^{\oplus c}}$. Thus $\varepsilon_a$ is injective; by step 3 it is surjective, so it is an isomorphism of $A_a$-modules ($(I_0/I_0^2)_a$ is free with basis $[f_1]/1,\dots,[f_c]/1$). Let $\lambda=\varepsilon_a\circ\psi':\Omega_a\to(I_0/I_0^2)_a$. Then $\lambda\circ(\mathrm d_\alpha)_a=\varepsilon_a\circ\psi'\circ(\mathrm d_\alpha)_a\circ\varepsilon_a\circ\varepsilon_a^{-1}=\varepsilon_a\circ\varepsilon_a^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$: the localized map $(\mathrm d_\alpha)_a$ has an $A_a$-linear left inverse.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CA (lemma-elkik), lines 270-273 ('Assumption (equation-strictly-standard-one) implies that the differential (I/I^2)_a -> (+) A_a dx_i has a left inverse'; the combination with the generation of step 3 written out)

proof.text: (A presentation of $A_a$ whose conormal map is split injective.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent] with its $A\to B$ our $R\to A$, its $P,\alpha$ our $P,\alpha$, $g=a$ and the lift $f=h$ of step 3 ($A_a$ is the ring of [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the case $M=A$ of [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]): the homomorphism of $R$-algebras $\beta:P[y]\to A_a$ equal to $\alpha$ followed by $A\to A_a$ on $P$ and with $\beta(y)=1/a$ is surjective, its kernel $K$ is generated by $I_0$ and $hy-1$, and by its clause (3) there are isomorphisms of $A_a$-modules $u_1:K/K^2\cong(I_0/I_0^2)_a\oplus A_a$ and $u_0:A_a\otimes_{P[y]}\Omega_{P[y]/R}\cong(A_a\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R})\oplus A_a$ with $u_0\circ\mathrm d_\beta=(\delta\oplus a)\circ u_1$, where $\mathrm d_\beta[g]=1\otimes\mathrm dg$ is the map of $\mathrm{NL}(\beta)$ and $\delta$ is the map of $\mathrm{NL}(\alpha)\otimes_AA_a$. Under the natural isomorphisms $(I_0/I_0^2)\otimes_AA_a\cong(I_0/I_0^2)_a$ and $\Omega\otimes_AA_a\cong\Omega_a$ of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-tensor] (with $\Omega\otimes_AA_a=A_a\otimes_P\Omega_{P/R}$ by associativity of base change [def-weil-module-base-change]), $\delta=\mathrm d_\alpha\otimes1$ corresponds to $(\mathrm d_\alpha)_a$ by the naturality clause of that node. With $\lambda$ of step 4, $\lambda'=u_1^{-1}\circ(\lambda\oplus a^{-1})\circ u_0$ satisfies $\lambda'\circ\mathrm d_\beta=u_1^{-1}\circ(\lambda\oplus a^{-1})\circ((\mathrm d_\alpha)_a\oplus a)\circ u_1=\mathrm{id}_{K/K^2}$. So $\mathrm d_\beta$ has an $A_a$-linear left inverse.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, proof of Lemma Tag 07CA (lemma-elkik), lines 273-274 ('Hence R -> A_a is smooth by definition and Algebra, Lemma 00S7'); the localization of the naive cotangent complex is taken here in the form of Algebra, Lemma Tag 08JZ (lemma-principal-localization-NL, algebra.tex line 35605), which gives a presentation of A_a

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Identify $P[y]$ with the polynomial ring $R[x_1,\dots,x_n,y]$ in $n+1$ variables [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. By step 5, $\beta:R[x_1,\dots,x_n,y]\to A_a$ is a surjective homomorphism of $R$-algebras whose kernel $K=(f_1,\dots,f_m,hy-1)$ is finitely generated, and its map $\mathrm d_\beta:K/K^2\to A_a\otimes_{P[y]}\Omega_{P[y]/R}$ has an $A_a$-linear left inverse. By [lem-weil-pbc-presentation-split-conormal-smooth], $A_a$ is a smooth $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] for the $R$-algebra structure through $\beta$, which is $R\to A\to A_a$ since $\beta$ restricted to $P$ is the $R$-algebra map $\alpha$ followed by $A\to A_a$. This is the claim.
